scenario.title: Mars: A Voice Beyond the Ridge
scenario.premise: A damaged landing strands a small expedition. Recovery becomes a rescue, then a return journey carrying people and evidence. This is an engineering story with recovered qualified systems, not real survival instructions.

stage.title: A voice above the ridge
stage.speaker: Mission Control
stage.motivation: We lost your signal on landing. Repair the radio and put a powered signal above the ridge. We are listening.
stage.travelText: We take the useful equipment onward to a voice above the ridge, leaving the earlier work where it stands.

objectives.text: Place a powered radio or directed optical beacon on Contact ridge.

stage.title: The sky is closing
stage.speaker: Weather officer
stage.motivation: Dust is obscuring the route. Restore the station so we can watch for a clear interval, and protect our spare controller before we move on.
stage.travelText: The mapped instrument apron is a short drive from the outcrop. We take the field kit and leave the sampling bench where it stands.

areas.label: What the cliff can tell us

things.label: Solar charger
things.description: The working solar charging unit recovered earlier. Its matched output can power the station recorder.

things.label: Motor controller
things.description: An intact spare drive controller in its open mounting cradle. The exposed electronics need an enclosure before travelling through blowing dust.

things.label: Annotated map
things.description: The terrain map with the outcrop observations and known routes marked on it.

things.label: Sensor mast
things.description: A complete calibrated weather sensor head on its mast. Its wind vane was detached for storage; temperature and pressure sensors are already protected inside the assembly.

things.label: Wind vane
things.description: The detached vane from this station. Its keyed hub fits the sensor mast.

things.label: Sensor logger
things.description: A complete weather recorder with its cable attached. It plugs into the station to record how conditions change over time.

things.label: Filter mesh
things.description: A sheet of replaceable equipment filter material. On its own it is too loose to protect the controller.

things.label: Vented enclosure
things.description: A controller enclosure with designed cooling vents and a frame for replaceable filter mesh.

locations.label: Weather apron
locations.description: Open ground clear of the station buildings, where the sensors can observe local weather without their shelter blocking the wind.

cacheNarrative.label: Weather-station service cabinet
cacheNarrative.narrative: The mothballed station was stored sensibly: its calibrated sensor mast, detached vane and complete logger are here together. A service enclosure and filter material can protect our spare controller.

stage.title: A voice in the static
stage.speaker: Orbital control
stage.motivation: The survey crew missed their last check-in. This relay can hear beyond the ridge. Bring it back on the air—we need to find out what happened.
stage.travelText: The weather record gives us a route to the relay knoll. We bring the map and leave the station measuring conditions behind us.

areas.label: What the cliff can tell us

objectives.text: Bring the working relay onto the knoll and establish contact.

things.label: Weather route map
things.description: Your terrain map annotated with the observed window of better visibility toward the old relay.

things.label: Relay transceiver
things.description: The largely intact site relay. Its service indicator identifies a blown replaceable fuse; its internal filters and wiring are already fitted.

things.label: Spare fuse
things.description: The matched replacement from the relay’s service pouch. The relay indicator identifies the failed fuse; this is not a generic repair for every electrical fault.

things.label: Directional antenna
things.description: The relay’s assembled directional antenna with its matched feed connector. Its bracket and feedline are already attached.

things.label: Relay powerpack
things.description: The intact site battery module, stored charged, with its regulator and protection circuits already built in.

locations.label: Relay knoll
locations.description: A raised, unobstructed radio site with a clear view beyond the ridge.

cacheNarrative.label: Relay maintenance cabinet
cacheNarrative.narrative: The relay itself is still here, with its complete antenna and charged powerpack stored beside it. Its service pouch holds a matched fuse; the fault indicator points to the old one.

output.message: Relay. Replace the identified blown fuse in the intact relay transceiver. Its internal radio circuits are already assembled.

stage.motivation: The survey crew missed their last check-in. This relay can hear beyond the ridge. Bring it back on the air—we need to find out what happened.
stage.travelText: The weather record gives us a route to the relay knoll. We bring the map and leave the station measuring conditions behind us.

areas.label: What the cliff can tell us

objectives.text: Bring the working relay onto the knoll and establish contact.

things.label: Weather route map
things.description: Your terrain map annotated with the observed window of better visibility toward the old relay.

things.label: Relay transceiver
things.description: The largely intact site relay. Its service indicator identifies a blown replaceable fuse; its internal filters and wiring are already fitted.

things.label: Spare fuse
things.description: The matched replacement from the relay’s service pouch. The relay indicator identifies the failed fuse; this is not a generic repair for every electrical fault.

things.label: Relay
things.description: A repaired radio relay awaiting its ready antenna and powerpack. No need to assemble its internal circuits.

things.label: Rescue route
things.description: The crew’s landmark matched to your weather route map. It marks the disabled crawler and the short recovery route to the service refuge.

locations.label: Relay knoll
locations.description: A raised, unobstructed radio site with a clear view beyond the ridge.

cacheNarrative.label: Relay maintenance cabinet
cacheNarrative.narrative: The relay itself is still here, with its complete antenna and charged powerpack stored beside it. Its service pouch holds a matched fuse; the fault indicator points to the old one.

output.message: Placed.

stage.title: Not the only ones stranded
stage.speaker: Survey crew
stage.motivation: Our cabin is intact, but its drive has failed. The refuge is a short way along the route. Prepare it, then bring us there in the crawler—repair its drive or tow us. A hot meal would be welcome.
stage.travelText: The message and map lead to the disabled crawler and the service refuge farther along the recovery route. We bring the rover and recovery kit; the working relay stays on its knoll.

areas.label: What the cliff can tell us

objectives.text: Get the crew into shelter and give them a hot meal.

things.label: Toolkit
things.description: The expedition’s service tools and diagnostic meter, suitable for inspecting the matched spare drive before fitting it.

things.label: Heater
things.description: The expedition’s compatible enclosed electric heater. It can warm the refuge or an existing food pouch.

things.label: Pressure patch
things.description: A qualified repair patch from the habitat kit, intended for the marked fabric seam damage—not for arbitrary pressure-vessel repairs.

things.label: Rover
things.description: A wheeled chassis is a recognizable rover with unfilled component slots.

things.label: Recovery rope
things.description: Rated vehicle-recovery rope, packed separately from its matching tow eye.

things.label: Tow eye
things.description: The matching rated recovery attachment for the rope and rover.

things.label: Spare drive
things.description: The crawler’s matched replacement drive module. Inspect it with the toolkit before attaching its coupling.

things.label: Drive coupling
things.description: The matched mechanical connection between the serviced spare drive and this crawler.

things.label: Service shelter
things.description: A field refuge a short way along the recovery route from the disabled crawler. Its life support is intact, but a documented seam tear needs the pressure patch before the crew can shelter here.

things.label: Disabled crawler
things.description: The crew’s intact mobile cabin with a failed drive. Repair the drive, or tow the cabin along the gentle recovery route with the equipped rover.

things.label: Bedding
things.description: The crew’s clean folded bedding for their camp bed.

things.label: Soup pouch
things.description: An intact prepared meal from the crew’s stores. Warm it before putting it in the insulated flask.

things.label: Insulated flask
things.description: An empty food flask that will keep the warmed meal ready while the crew is brought to shelter.

things.label: Folding bed
things.description: A complete camp bed. It needs bedding before it will be a comfortable resting place.

cacheNarrative.label: Survey refuge and crawler stores
cacheNarrative.narrative: The crew are waiting in their intact crawler cabin. Its service compartment holds a spare drive and towing equipment. The nearby field refuge, a short way along the recovery route, has bedding and food, but needs preparation before the crew can move in.

output.message: Tow line. Fit the rope to the rated recovery eye.

args: Voluntary stop at provisioned refuge, stage 7 goals satisfied, not campaign ending. Fresh checkpoint play: 26 accepted actions, 23 combinations (18 creations, 5 installations), 2 advances, 1 placement; no rejected attempts, hints, undo, moves or visits. Weather observation to route map coherent; clear descriptions made combinations intuitive but often routine. Relay repeated base-plus-two-slots pattern. Missing-crew hook motivated continuation. Relay onto knoll first generated recording but left contact objective false; repeating identical drop later placed it and satisfied goal, confusing bureaucratic extra gesture. Original parts and old object states remaining after transformation felt cluttered/inconsistent with consumed installations. Rescue tow versus repair choice welcome; chose tow. Getting intact cabin to prepared refuge was satisfying; bedding and soup were literal checklist. Crew warm and fed gives enough closure to stop rather than start another chain. Logical interface trial only, no graphics or human-fun claim.
